findings.title: Device limit can be bypassed by retrying after a rejected tag
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI, the device ID is written to localCache before CreateOrUpdateDevice is called. If CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached on the first attempt, the cache entry remains. A retry for the same device within the cache TTL hits the cached entry and returns nil before reaching the store, so Anonymous.Authenticate no longer sees ErrDeviceLimitReached and anonymous authentication succeeds. This makes the configured device limit bypassable after one retry, and the rejected device is never recorded.

findings.title: Device limit enforcement is not atomic
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice enforces the limit with a separate CountDevices call followed by an insert/upsert, with no transaction, row lock, or serialization. Two different new devices can concurrently both observe count < deviceLimit and both insert, so the stored number of devices can exceed the configured limit. For example, with deviceLimit=1, two concurrent new device requests can both count 0 and both insert, leaving 2 devices.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication now synchronously writes to the device store
findings.body: Anonymous.Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously on the authentication path. Previously this work was fire-and-forget in a background goroutine. With the default anonymousDeviceLimit=0 this feature is not even active, but every cache-missing anonymous request must still wait for a database upsert before authentication completes. This adds database write latency to anonymous login/page-load paths and is a performance regression for all anonymous traffic.

findings.title: updateDevice can falsely report ErrDeviceLimitReached for an existing device
findings.body: updateDevice treats RowsAffected() == 0 as proof that the device is missing or stale and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL, UPDATE RowsAffected is commonly the number of rows changed, not matched. If an existing row already has the same client_ip, user_agent, and updated_at values (for example, requests within the same second when the timestamp column has second precision), the update can affect 0 rows even though the device exists. The existing device is then rejected and anonymous authentication fails unexpectedly. The code should distinguish 'matched but unchanged' from 'not matched', such as by using CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS or checking existence separately.
